h: Coastal Days Out Beyond the Golf
p: Crazy golf is one of those things that works for almost everyone. Toddlers can bash the ball about, teenagers can get competitive, and grandparents can pull off the shot of the day. To keep things moving, agree a maximum number of shots per hole before you start, and save the arguments over the scorecard until afterwards.

If you're going as a family, earlier sessions are usually calmer and better for younger children. Groups of adults may prefer the livelier evening atmosphere, but check whether any age restrictions apply later on.

Bournemouth makes a great base for exploring the coast. Head east to Boscombe Pier and the stretch of beach around it, or carry on to Hengistbury Head, where a walk to the top rewards you with stunning views over Christchurch Harbour and the Isle of Wight on a clear day. Christchurch itself has a beautiful priory church and a pretty quay.

To the west, Poole Harbour is a vast natural harbour dotted with islands, and the chain ferry from Sandbanks takes you across to Studland. From there, you can walk to Old Harry Rocks, the famous chalk stacks at the start of the Jurassic Coast. Back in Bournemouth, the Oceanarium by the pier is a good wet-weather alternative for families. Pair it with a round of golf and you've got a rainy day sorted.
